title: Still vs. Yet & Possessives

expressions.example: Are you still here? I thought you left an hour ago!
Can you wait? I haven't finished yet.

expressions.meaning: Guarde para si / Não conte para ninguém.
expressions.example: It's a secret — keep it to yourself, please.
Stop! It's my turn to speak now.

sentences: Are you still working on the project?
I still don't understand this grammar rule.
She still lives with her parents.
Have you finished your homework yet?
My phone is on the table.
Their car is still in the garage.

grammar.title: STILL vs. YET + Possessive Adjectives
rules: STILL (Ainda — algo continua): ANTES do verbo principal ou ENTRE auxiliar e verbo principal
Ex: "I still don't know." / "Are you still here?" / "It's still raining."
YET (Ainda não / Já): NO FINAL da frase — usado em negativos e perguntas
Ex: "Have you finished yet?" / "I haven't eaten yet." / "She hasn't arrived yet."
Possessive Adjectives: sempre ANTES do substantivo — My, Your, His, Her, Its, Our, Their

rows: My book / Her car / Their house

quiz.q: ___ car is still in the garage. (they)
